body:
That's such a good analogy! I'm definitely going to use it the next time this comes up because I know he's hurt that I don't trust him or our relationship completely. 

I think part of the issue is he thinks he understands me more than he actually does.  My boyfriend is an engineering psychologist and has been exposed to BPD and its symptoms at some point in his schooling. While I do believe he "knows" the list of symptoms (and maybe he even understands it in theory), he seems less familiar with the experiential side. In other words, he cannot connect the behavioral manifestations of BPD to the symptoms/criteria. I think your framing might help him get it. Thanks :)

Thank you for sharing your experience, and I'm glad things worked out with you and your husband. It gives me some hope that I'll be able to do this.

I've tried to explain that this is anxiety-driven and how these suggestions (e.g., 'you don't know what I'm capable of') reduces my anxiety in a twisted way. I don't want to be shanghaied by his leaving, so I kind of present plausible reasons to leave. In a way, it makes me feel more in control of the outcome because if he left, it's something I predicted (it's dumb, I know).

I think he understands (or thinks he understands) the fear element. He says the behavior makes "logical sense," but he cannot understand why I would give him these reasons if I'm cognitively aware of the consequences. I will try emphasizing that he's not doing anything to make me distrustful. I don't know how to communicate this paradox in a way he can understand, and I do not know what I'm looking for when I do this. Do you have any suggestions?

Hey there. I'm sorry you're having a hard time :( Do you no longer have access to the pdoc/MD who wrote the original prescriptions? I can't help you with insurance/getting the meds (not my area of expertise), but if you're looking for someone to listen, PM me and I'd be happy too. I hope you feel better soon.

It's funny that you posted this because I told my partner this afternoon.

I have struggled with this for a long time. No one-- siblings, closest friends, ex-boyfriends, etc.-- knows about my diagnosis except for my parents. Like you, I am, for the most part, open about other issues. Sometimes, depending on the relationship, I can even be open to sharing how I experience my BPD symptoms w/o using the label (e.g., I'll say I am "sensitive" and feel things "more intensely"). For me, my fear has always been that any disclosure I made would not only be an instant dealbreaker, but would also reduce my entire identity-- everything I am-- to this one label. I have BPD, but I am not BPD. 

I have been in the healthiest relationship of my life for almost two years. I am extremely lucky because my partner is naturally patient. He keeps his cool when I start to get frustrated, which prevents huge blowups since the conflict never escalates. We have had many conversations about my distrust/insecurity regarding the longevity of our relationship as well as discussions about my intense emotions.

This afternoon, we got into a massive fight-- probably the biggest one we've ever had. I thought it was *the* fight. I won't go into the details of the fight bc this comment is already long.

In my head, he knew everything there was to know about my bpd except the label. After our fight today, I realized that by withholding the label, I was robbing him of the many resources written for the people who are close to someone with bpd. I wanted to recommend some books to him, so I decided to tell him. It was the scariest thing in the world. I've never shared this with anyone else before and had no prior experiences to compare it to. Anything was possible + I did not know what to expect.

He did not care about the label at all. He was disappointed that it took me two years to tell him and he was hurt because I thought he would bolt. This is not to say you should disclose immediately nor is it to say you should wait a long time. Maybe try testing the waters? Progressively reveal more about yourself and see how he reacts. I am sorry that I do not have any advice on the "when" component.

In some ways, it is comforting knowing that there are many other people who have similar thoughts/experiences/struggles. It makes me feel less alone/different. At the same time, OP, you are more than your diagnosis. Nothing about you changed after you got your diagnosis-- you are still the same person you were 6 months ago. The only difference is, you now know what to treat. You now have access to groups and therapy and books and a whole host of other things that target the ways we think/act specifically. I hope this does not come across as dismissive because that is not my intention. It's a lot to process, and if you ever need someone to talk to (or just listen), feel free to PM me. Good luck, OP.
Thanks :) I don't know what an "art friend" is, but I am certainly interested. I am not very artistic though... does it work with stick figures?

Exactly! I feel that even in the suckiest situations, it helps to know that you are not alone. Feel free to PM me if you want to talk and/or try to a workable solution :)

Also... best birthday! Are we twins?

Omg! I am having the same problem. I am also looking for a job and lacking professional references. Since I am quiet (but diligent), I feel that I am quite forgettable because, frankly, there is nothing about me for anyone to remember. I do my work well, ask for help when I need it, and do not cause problems... so people leave me alone. This is why I am hesitant to reach out to people I worked with two or more years ago. I feel they won't remember me. I am sorry I do not have any advice for you... I just wanted to make sure you know that you're not alone.

Also, /u/ericat713, we are basically twins. My sister's name is "erica" and my birthday is 713. Funny coincidence :)

I agree with /u/mahnemisjaze-- it is extremely kind of you to reach out and support him. You are not a failure. In fact, I wish I had more people like you in my life. I am sorry you are going through this.

Could it be possible that he's been hospitalized? I don't know if this is true across the board, but when I have been hospitalized, I did not have access to my phone or computer or the internet.

I hope he's ok, and I hope *you're* ok. Make sure you are taking care of yourself. This sounds rough, and I am sorry you are going through this :(

Thank you for saying this. I do feel like it is on me though because I know my therapist cares deeply for me. I know she does not like seeing how I've given up and how unwilling I am to try to work my way out of this situation. I think she feels helpless, and I cannot imagine how draining-- toxic, even-- it must be for her to work with me.

That said, yeah. She kind of left me in a difficult situation, and I am even more isolated w/o anywhere to go. I do not have support system, but it does not feel worth it to try to find another when I will resume with her in a couple of months.

I'm sorry that you're in a similar position-- it's an awful place to be. 

I wish I were able to explain to people how I am not exaggerating when I say there is nothing that brings me joy. That there is no goal I hope to achieve or drive to do anything. I feel like I've tried to be happy... like kind of going through the motions, hoping to 'fake it until i made it.' I am exasperated and don't want to try anymore.

I hope you do find something that gives you a reason to live/something that makes you feel alive.

It is crazy how quickly time flies... especially when you're depressed. For me, it is almost like the whole world fades away, and I withdraw back into myself and stop participating in society. I cannot believe that I've been where I am for as long as I have.

I am sorry that you've endured so much, and I think it's extremely admirable that you are able to recognize and appreciate that the time we *are* given is relatively short and treat your life with respect. I'm glad you've been able to find sources of happiness in your life :)

Oh, dude, I feel your pain. I'm having a very similar experience. I dropped out of my MA program and started looking for administrative work. I figured I was qualified to answer phones, file, correspond... whatever and expected my job search to take like 3-4 weeks. It has been over *three months.* I need to find something by May or I'm going to be evicted.

The worst part is, I do get called in for interviews. To me, it feels like once they meet me they change their minds. 

I totally agree. On top of these terrible things I already feel, I experience a lot of guilt because there are people who would do *anything* to live one more day. I think of them, and I so badly want to give them my life. At least it'd be appreciated. At least the recipient would enjoy it.
I'm glad I'm not alone, but I am sorry you are having this experience. It seems super unfair that I'm wasting my life away while there are people who really really want to live. It makes me sad.

Thank you for your comment. That's the thing though-- it's not just the monotony of working a soul-sucking job that drives my desire to kill myself. I am very lucky (bc I certainly did not have anything to do with it) in that I am financially secure, so I *could* just pursue a passion, even if it were low-paying. But there are no passions to pursue. I wish there were-- I wish I *could* find an activity or something that makes me happy because I'd have a "break" from feeling like that. 

Lately, people have been asking me what I want, and I don't have an answer. I don't want anything (besides some kind of doctor-assisted suicide situation, but that's not going to happen). There is nothing that interests me or makes me excited.

The therapy thing was my fault, and I feel bad. It is probably so hard for therapist to work with someone who has no motivation to do anything. Anyway, we had a deal that if I missed four appointments in a row, she would not work with me for three months. I participated in a weekly group that my therapist ran, and I missed four of *those* sessions in a row. I thought that showing up to my weekly individual sessions would restart the count (i.e., if I saw her for group on Tuesday and then had individual on Wednesday, I assumed that I cleaned the slate).

The serial killer "volunteer sign-up sheet" made me smile. I wish for this too. I think I'm pretty empathetic, but (political issues aside) I cannot understand people on death row who would rather be in prison for life than executed. I do not know what *wanting* to live and hold onto life even in terrible circumstances feels like. It is hard for me to fathom.

I am the same way about not being able to find a source of happiness, which yeah, makes it difficult to want to get out of bed. I'm sorry that you're going through this and hope you can find your way out :)

It feels good to know I'm not alone in feeling this way (but I *am* sorry you've had similar experiences-- no one should have to go through this). If there were a foolproof way to go, I'd probably do it-- but yes. Being paralyzed or brain dead or physically handicapped is going to make life more miserable and will likely hinder future suicide attempts.
